tagline: Up into the border woods and lakes, then down to prairie.
intro: Three miles north of Rolla, by St. John, County Highway 43 starts west into the Turtle Mountains, crosses US 281 and carries on as State Highway 43 to Highway 14. It climbs past farmsteads and pasture, clear lakes and wooded wildlife areas, then comes down into the foothills with the prairie laid out below.

The Turtle Mountains are a plateau standing 300 to 400 feet above the country around them, wooded in ash, aspen, oak and birch and scattered with lakes. They are the traditional territory of the Plains Ojibwe and part of the Métis homeland.

moments.title: International Peace Garden
moments.text: Up US 281 at the border, visitors cross between the two countries at will inside the garden, then go through customs on the way out, even when heading home.

moments.title: Lake Metigoshe
moments.text: Settlers first called it Fish Lake, and two of its north-shore bays reach over the line into Canada.
